description:
Rule (maintainer, 2026-10-13): the HexDocs extras (mix.exs @guides and @reference: README, the guides, scope.md, performance.md, language.md, compile-errors.md, the cheatsheet) are for a user of the library. ADR links and beadwork ticket ids are for someone developing defk and do not belong there. Counted on 2026-10-13: performance.md 282 ticket ids and 8 ADR mentions, language.md 27 ids, scope.md 10, measuring.md 5, testing.md 3, cheatsheet 3, getting-started.md 2 ids and 2 ADR mentions, runtime-contract.md 2 ids and 3 ADR mentions, deploying.md 1 id and 4 ADR mentions.

Decide and do:
- performance.md: it is written for future maintainers ('what is fast on the BEAM, for future us', every entry has a Source line of ticket ids). Either take it out of the extras (link it from docs/project.md by its GitHub URL, as beam-nifs.md is) or keep it as a user page and move every Source attribution into a maintainer appendix outside HexDocs. The first is cheaper and honest about its audience.
- scope.md 'Not yet': test/scope_doc_test.exs requires a ticket id per bullet. Replace the ids with plain statements of what is planned, and change the test to check the planned codes only; the ids live in beadwork.
- language.md, the guides and the cheatsheet: replace each ticket id with the statement it stands for (or drop it where it only credits the work), and each ADR link with the decision's one-line substance or a GitHub URL to docs/project.md where a maintainer can continue.
- Add a check to test/docs_checks_test.exs so an extra with a defk-xxx id or an adr/ link fails the suite, so this stays true.

Done when: no extra contains a ticket id or an ADR reference, the new check is in the suite, and mix ci is green.
title: HexDocs pages must not reference ADRs or tickets: they are for users, not maintainers
